<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

A seat's type appears in `pij list --json` and `pij directory`, beside every existing field; a seat holding roles of two types is flagged with the split; authority is unchanged.

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- The operator can tell a coder from an expert from a human window in the list and the view.

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- Removing or renaming any JSON field (a redundant one is proposed as a later cleanup).
- Recomputing authority from the type: `seat_role_for` and the prime designation are untouched.

<a id="research-context"></a>

## Research Context

Seats are listed by GET /v1/seats (crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs) and joined to their seat role by `join_roles` (http/role.rs); community holdings are `community_assignments` (crates/store/src/community.rs). The view is built in community/directory.rs and its actions in community/picture.rs. The OMP and Copilot extensions read `pij list` JSON; new fields are additive. Design change from the first cut: the type rides the role document's pointer (`community_pointers`, written after every directory commit and rebuilt from the branch head) rather than a column on every holding, which would have touched every `Assignment` literal and needed a restamp on each type edit.

<a id="execution-guardrails"></a>

## Execution Guardrails

- Cost: migration 0052 is one ALTER at boot. Each directory write already records its pointers; it now also reads each role document it committed once (in-process, no launch). Every `/v1/seats` call adds one indexed store query (open holdings joined to pointers), so it also rides the calls that poll the roster (federation fan-in, about once a second per peer, and the extension roster); never per seat, no file read, no launch. No loop, poll or timer is added.
- No permission rule changes (PRD 003); no daemon enforcement of a type's rules; no existing JSON field removed or renamed.
- Builds nice-19 through `just shared-build`, one at a time.
